rows.text: The Assembly's item of 28 August 2013 calls Lord Tu'iha'ateiho 'THE Acting Speaker of the Legislative Assembly' at a time when 'Speaker Lord Fakafanua was leaving the country' for a Commonwealth Parliamentary Association meeting in the Cayman Islands; members urged him to continue as Acting Speaker until the Speaker resumed duty.
rows.uncertainty: Acting service during the Speaker's absence: a claim only, never a holder. Its start and end are not stated.

rows.text: The same item reports that Lord Tu'iha'ateiho 'announced his resignation from the post yesterday morning' (27 August 2013), apologised for any wrongdoing 'while performing his duty as Deputy Speaker' and said he felt he could not handle taking the leadership role, and that members asked him to defer it.
rows.uncertainty: An announcement, not a stated acceptance. The item never names the post he resigned from: its headline and the members' appeals point to the acting leadership role, while his apology mentions his duty as Deputy Speaker. The same item says he resumed duty as Acting Speaker after the tea break (to_tuihaateiho_resumed_acting_speaker_20130828).

rows.text: The same item, headed 'Deputy Speaker remains Acting Speaker of Parliament', states that 'After the tea break, Lord Tu'iha'ateiho resumed duty as the Acting Speaker after resignation.'
rows.uncertainty: Continuation of acting service: a claim only, never a holder. attested_on is the item's date; the item implies but does not state that the tea break fell on the same sitting day as the announcement of 27 August.

rows.text: The same item styles 'Speaker Lord Fakafanua', who was leaving the country to attend a Commonwealth Parliamentary Association meeting in the Cayman Islands.
rows.uncertainty: A mid-term attestation only; his absence is not a vacancy.
